analysis.subject: finance
analysis.pageCoverage: Page covers teen saving conversations including how much to save, estimating emergency expenses, choosing safe insured accounts, deciding about retirement matching, and compound interest examples showing benefits of starting early

overview.headline: Teen saving habits for emergency funds and early investing

keyPoints.point: Teens can aim to save 10 percent of earnings and keep at least three months of living expenses saved for an emergency
keyPoints.quote: “A good rule to live by is to save 10 percent of what you earn, and have at least three months’ worth of living expenses saved up in case of an emergency.”

keyPoints.point: Keeping money in a federally insured bank or credit union helps keep savings in a safe place
keyPoints.quote: Talk about how to keep money in a safe place, like a federally insured bank or credit union.

keyPoints.point: Setting aside $100 every year starting at age 14 can grow to about $23,000 by age 65 through compounding
keyPoints.quote: If they set aside $100 every year starting at age 14, they'd have about $23,000 at age 65.

keyPoints.point: Employers may provide matching contributions as an incentive to save and reaching the maximum matching contribution is smart
keyPoints.quote: Some employers provide matching contributions as an incentive to save, so it’s smart to save at least enough for the maximum matching contribution.

keyTerms.gloss: a regular plan for setting aside money so funds are readily available for emergencies
keyTerms.quote: Explain to your child that one goal of a savings program is to have money readily available in case an emergency occurs.

keyTerms.gloss: interest earned on both the original saved money and the accumulated interest
keyTerms.quote: Compound interest is when your child earns interest on both the money they save and the interest they earn.

keyTerms.gloss: protection where deposits are federally insured by the banking system for safety
keyTerms.quote: Talk about how to keep money in a safe place, like a federally insured bank or credit union.

keyTerms.gloss: employer payments that provide matching funds as an incentive to save for retirement
keyTerms.quote: Some employers provide matching contributions as an incentive to save, so it’s smart to save at least enough for the maximum matching contribution.
